text.en: There is one more sheet, and for ten days this archive had it filed as a photograph of a face. It is a torn page of German typing: fifteen numbered families, with birth dates and street addresses in Kraków, Sosnowiec, Bielsko and Lublin, and at the foot, in pencil, an address in Bucharest — care of Ing. L. Filderman, Strada Paleologu — for Jakob Griffel. Dr Jacob Griffel was the Agudath Israel and Vaad Hatzalah rescue representative in Istanbul, one of the few channels through which Orthodox rescue money and papers reached occupied Europe. When Basia showed the sheet to Ms Manowska of the Pilecki Institute, who researches the wartime 'passports of life', she recognised it at sight as belonging to the operation that issued foreign passports to Jews, and asked at once where it had been found and what its reference number was. Six of the fifteen entries are the brothers and sisters of David's own family — the children of Isaac Chaim Griffel — and the birth dates match this family's tree to the month. This was a man in Bucharest trying to get his own relatives onto paper that might count as a passport. Of the people on that sheet, Samuel lived and died in Brooklyn in 1999; Osias Heinrich lived and died in Jersey City in 1968; Menashe Karmel lived until 1989. Schalom, his wife and both of his little daughters were murdered in 1942. Schmul Rosenbojm was murdered at Lublin in 1942 and his son Izajasz in 1943. Whether a single passport was ever issued against this list, and whether it reached anybody in time, is not something this archive can say.
text.he: יש עוד דף אחד, ובמשך עשרה ימים הארכיון הזה תייק אותו כתצלום של פנים. זהו דף קרוע של הקלדה בגרמנית: חמש-עשרה משפחות ממוספרות, עם תאריכי לידה וכתובות רחוב בקרקוב, בסוסנוביץ, בביילסקו ובלובלין, ובתחתיתו, בעיפרון, כתובת בבוקרשט — אצל אינג׳ ל׳ פילדרמן, רחוב פלאולוגו — עבור יעקב גריפל. ד״ר יעקב גריפל היה נציג ההצלה של אגודת ישראל וּועד ההצלה באיסטנבול, אחד הצינורות המעטים שדרכם הגיעו כספי הצלה וניירות לאירופה הכבושה. כשהראתה בסיה את הדף לגב׳ מנובסקה ממכון פילצקי, החוקרת את ״דרכונות החיים״, היא זיהתה מיד שהוא שייך למבצע הנפקת הדרכונים הזרים ליהודים, ושאלה על אתר היכן נמצא ומה מספר הסימוכין שלו. שש מתוך חמש-עשרה הרשומות הן אחיו ואחיותיו של בית אביו של דוד — ילדיו של יצחק חיים גריפל — ותאריכי הלידה תואמים את עץ המשפחה עד כדי חודש. זה היה אדם בבוקרשט שניסה להעלות את קרוביו שלו על נייר שאולי ייחשב דרכון. מבין האנשים שברשימה: שמואל חי ונפטר בברוקלין ב-1999; אושיאס היינריך חי ונפטר בג׳רזי סיטי ב-1968; מנשה כרמל חי עד 1989. שלום, אשתו ושתי בנותיו הקטנות נרצחו ב-1942. שמואל רוזנבוים נרצח בלובלין ב-1942 ובנו ישעיהו ב-1943. האם הונפק אי-פעם דרכון אחד על סמך הרשימה הזו, והאם הגיע למישהו בזמן — זאת הארכיון הזה אינו יודע לומר.
text.pl: Jest jeszcze jedna kartka, którą archiwum przez dziesięć dni trzymało jako fotografię twarzy. To podarta strona maszynopisu po niemiecku: piętnaście ponumerowanych rodzin, z datami urodzenia i adresami w Krakowie, Sosnowcu, Bielsku i Lublinie, a u dołu, ołówkiem, adres w Bukareszcie — na ręce inż. L. Fildermana, Strada Paleologu — dla Jakuba Griffla, przedstawiciela Agudat Israel i Waad Hacala w Stambule. Gdy Basia pokazała ją pani Manowskiej z Instytutu Pileckiego, badaczce „paszportów życia”, ta rozpoznała ją od razu jako materiał akcji paszportowej i natychmiast zapytała o miejsce znalezienia i sygnaturę. Sześć z piętnastu pozycji to rodzeństwo z domu ojca Dawida.
text.fr: Il reste une feuille, que cette archive a classée dix jours durant comme la photographie d'un visage. C'est une page dactylographiée en allemand, déchirée : quinze familles numérotées, avec dates de naissance et adresses à Cracovie, Sosnowiec, Bielsko et Lublin, et au bas, au crayon, une adresse à Bucarest — aux bons soins de l'ing. L. Filderman, Strada Paleologu — pour Jakob Griffel, représentant du sauvetage d'Agudath Israel et du Vaad Hatzalah à Istanbul. Montrée à Mme Manowska de l'Institut Pilecki, qui étudie les « passeports de la vie », elle l'a reconnue aussitôt comme relevant de l'opération des passeports étrangers. Six des quinze entrées sont les frères et sœurs de la maison paternelle de David.

sources: The sheet itself — held in this archive as doc_griffel_rescue_list_bucharest, received from Jacob with the Griffel family library on 10 August 2026
Ms Manowska, Pilecki Institute, reported by Basia on 19 August 2026
Cross-checked line by line against griffel_tree.json (390 people) and against the Pilecki Institute's published Ładoś List, 2,987 entries parsed in full

title.en: Katowice — and a separation nobody recorded
title.pl: Katowice — i rozstanie, którego nikt nie zapisał
title.fr: Katowice — et une séparation que personne n’a notée

text.en: The war ended and they came west with the repatriation, to Katowice. On 1 July 1946 Lusia and Shimon each filed a survivor-registration card at the Katowice committee — cards 151738 and 151337, mother and son, one after the other.
text.he: המלחמה נגמרה והם באו מערבה עם הריפטריאציה, לקטוביץ. ב-1 ביולי 1946 מילאו לוסיה ושמעון כל אחד כרטיס רישום ניצולים בוועד קטוביץ — כרטיסים 151738 ו-151337, אם ובנה, זה אחר זה.
text.pl: Wojna się skończyła i wrócili na zachód wraz z repatriacją, do Katowic. 1 lipca 1946 Łucja i Szymon złożyli w katowickim komitecie karty rejestracyjne ocalałych — numery 151738 i 151337, matka i syn, jedna po drugiej.
text.fr: La guerre finie, ils revinrent vers l’ouest avec le rapatriement, à Katowice. Le 1er juillet 1946, Lusia et Shimon déposèrent chacun une fiche d’enregistrement de survivant au comité de Katowice — nos 151738 et 151337, la mère et le fils, l’une après l’autre.

sources: CKŻP cards nr 151738 and nr 151337, Katowice, 1 July 1946

text.en: But David had been registered as a Displaced Person in Brussels since 9 April 1946 — three months earlier. On the day he was recorded in Belgium, his wife and son were still in Poland. He had gone ahead, and they followed later that year. The memoir says only that "the family reaches Brussels and stays in a hotel": one movement, everyone together. The two cards, held in this archive since May and never read against each other until August 2026, say otherwise. It is the first of the two separations in this story.
text.he: אך דוד היה רשום כעקור בבריסל כבר מ-9 באפריל 1946 — שלושה חודשים קודם. ביום שבו נרשם בבלגיה, אשתו ובנו היו עדיין בפולין. הוא הקדים, והם באו אחריו באותה שנה. היומן אומר רק ש״המשפחה מגיעה לבריסל ומתאכסנת במלון״: תנועה אחת, כולם יחד. שני הכרטיסים, שהיו בארכיון הזה מאז מאי ומעולם לא נקראו זה מול זה עד אוגוסט 2026, אומרים אחרת. זו הראשונה משתי הפרידות בסיפור הזה.
text.pl: Ale Dawid był zarejestrowany jako dipis w Brukseli już od 9 kwietnia 1946 — trzy miesiące wcześniej. W dniu, w którym zapisano go w Belgii, jego żona i syn byli jeszcze w Polsce. Pojechał przodem, a oni dołączyli później tego samego roku. Pamiętnik mówi tylko, że „rodzina dociera do Brukseli i mieszka w hotelu”: jeden ruch, wszyscy razem. Obie karty, w tym archiwum od maja i nigdy dotąd nieprzeczytane obok siebie, mówią co innego. To pierwsze z dwóch rozstań w tej historii.
text.fr: Mais David était enregistré comme personne déplacée à Bruxelles depuis le 9 avril 1946 — trois mois plus tôt. Le jour où il fut inscrit en Belgique, sa femme et son fils étaient encore en Pologne. Il est parti devant, ils ont suivi plus tard cette année-là. Le mémoire dit seulement que « la famille arrive à Bruxelles et loge à l’hôtel » : un seul mouvement, tous ensemble. Les deux fiches, dans ces archives depuis mai et jamais lues l’une contre l’autre, disent autre chose. C’est la première des deux séparations de cette histoire.

title.en: Brussels — and Dov
title.pl: Bruksela — i Dov
title.fr: Bruxelles — et Dov

text.en: And she was there first. For as long as this archive has existed, the earliest Brussels record in it was David’s Displaced Persons card of 9 April 1946. On 19 August 2026 Basia sent Lusia’s: she registered in the same city on 26 DECEMBER 1945, three and a half months earlier, signing it "Rapaport Lea" while the clerk filed her under her maiden name. Two days later a Jewish aid society asked the Belgians to let her stay six months; on 7 February 1946 the Ministry of Justice agreed, on condition the permission was marked "with a view to emigration" — she could be in Belgium only while waiting to leave it. She was living at 250 rue des Coteaux in Schaerbeek. Dov was born under that arrangement. Her card carries two things nobody can yet explain: it says she came from a camp in Prague, which appears nowhere else and not in her own book; and it gives her birthplace as Haifa, Palestine. She was born in Bolechów. David’s card of the same series names Cieszyn, also wrong. Two cards, two wrong birthplaces — and on hers, under destination, the word Palestine.
text.he: והיא הייתה שם ראשונה. מאז קיומו של הארכיון הזה, הרשומה הבריסלית המוקדמת ביותר שבו הייתה כרטיס העקורים של דוד מ-9 באפריל 1946. ב-19 באוגוסט 2026 שלחה בסיה את כרטיסה של לוסיה: היא נרשמה באותה עיר ב-26 בדצמבר 1945, שלושה חודשים וחצי קודם לכן, וחתמה ״רפפורט לאה״ בעוד הפקיד מתייק אותה בשם נעוריה. יומיים לאחר מכן ביקשה אגודת סיוע יהודית מן הבלגים להתיר לה שהייה של שישה חודשים; ב-7 בפברואר 1946 הסכים משרד המשפטים, בתנאי שההיתר יסומן ״לקראת הגירה״ — מותר לה לשהות בבלגיה רק כל עוד היא ממתינה לעזוב אותה. היא התגוררה ברחוב דה קוטו 250 בסכרבק. דב נולד תחת ההסדר הזה. כרטיסה נושא שני דברים שאיש אינו יכול עדיין להסביר: כתוב בו שהגיעה ממחנה בפראג, דבר שאינו מופיע בשום מקום אחר ואף לא בספרה שלה; ומקום לידתה רשום כחיפה, פלשתינה. היא נולדה בבולחוב. בכרטיסו של דוד מאותה סדרה רשום צ׳ישין, גם הוא שגוי. שני כרטיסים, שני מקומות לידה שגויים — ובכרטיסה, תחת יעד, המילה פלשתינה.
text.pl: I to ona była tam pierwsza. Najwcześniejszym brukselskim dokumentem w tym archiwum była karta dipisa Dawida z 9 kwietnia 1946. 19 sierpnia 2026 Basia przysłała kartę Łucji: zarejestrowała się w tym samym mieście 26 GRUDNIA 1945, trzy i pół miesiąca wcześniej, podpisując się "Rapaport Lea". 7 lutego 1946 Ministerstwo Sprawiedliwości zezwoliło jej na pobyt "w celu emigracji". Mieszkała przy 250 rue des Coteaux w Schaerbeek. Tam urodził się Dow. Karta mówi też, że przyjechała z obozu w Pradze — czego nie ma nigdzie indziej — i podaje jako miejsce urodzenia Hajfę w Palestynie. Urodziła się w Bolechowie.
text.fr: Et c’est elle qui est arrivée la première. Le plus ancien document bruxellois de ces archives était la fiche de David, du 9 avril 1946. Le 19 août 2026, Basia a envoyé celle de Lusia : elle s’est enregistrée dans la même ville le 26 DÉCEMBRE 1945, trois mois et demi plus tôt, signant « Rapaport Lea ». Le 7 février 1946, le ministère de la Justice l’autorise à séjourner « en vue de l’émigration ». Elle habitait 250 rue des Coteaux, à Schaerbeek. Dov y est né. Sa fiche dit aussi qu’elle venait d’un camp à Prague — introuvable ailleurs — et donne pour lieu de naissance Haïfa, Palestine. Elle est née à Bolechów.

text.en: David's Displaced Persons card describes a forestry engineer, Polish nationality stripped in 1942, speaking Polish, Italian, German, Czech and Russian. It is the only document that reaches across from the war into what came after.
text.he: כרטיס העקורים של דוד מתאר מהנדס יערות, אזרחותו הפולנית נשללה ב-1942, דובר פולנית, איטלקית, גרמנית, צ׳כית ורוסית. זהו המסמך היחיד המגשר מן המלחמה אל מה שבא אחריה.
text.pl: Karta dipisa Dawida opisuje inżyniera leśnictwa, pozbawionego obywatelstwa polskiego w 1942, mówiącego po polsku, włosku, niemiecku, czesku i rosyjsku. To jedyny dokument, który przerzuca most z wojny w to, co nastąpiło po niej.
text.fr: La fiche de personne déplacée de David décrit un ingénieur forestier, déchu de la nationalité polonaise en 1942, parlant polonais, italien, allemand, tchèque et russe. C’est le seul document qui fasse le pont entre la guerre et ce qui suivit.

text.en: Dov Bernard Rapaport was born in Brussels on 28 August 1946. No Belgian birth registration is held in this archive — it is the easiest missing document of all, and only he can request it, as the person the record belongs to.
text.he: דב ברנרד רפפורט נולד בבריסל ב-28 באוגוסט 1946. אין בארכיון הזה רישום לידה בלגי — זהו המסמך החסר הקל ביותר מכולם, ורק הוא יכול לבקש אותו, כאדם שהרשומה שייכת לו.
text.pl: Dov Bernard Rapaport urodził się w Brukseli 28 sierpnia 1946. W tym archiwum nie ma belgijskiego aktu urodzenia — to najłatwiejszy do zdobycia brakujący dokument, a poprosić o niego może tylko on sam, jako osoba, której zapis dotyczy.
text.fr: Dov Bernard Rapaport est né à Bruxelles le 28 août 1946. Aucun acte de naissance belge ne figure dans ces archives — c’est le document manquant le plus facile à obtenir, et lui seul peut le demander, en tant que personne concernée.

text.en: One thing about Belgium had been sitting in plain sight. David's aunt Jente — his father's sister — spent the war in Liège, at Rue Lairesse 88, registered as a Polish national. Her daughter Szewa married there in 1941, a marriage this archive already held without seeing what stood behind it. So when David and Lusia reached Belgium in 1946, it was not a country the family had never been to: part of it had lived there straight through the occupation, a hundred kilometres from Brussels. Whether David went where he had people, no document in our hands says. It is worth asking and it is not worth inventing.
text.he: דבר אחד בנוגע לבלגיה ישב לנגד עינינו כל העת. דודתו של דוד, ינטה — אחות אביו — עברה את המלחמה בליאז׳, ברחוב לרס 88, רשומה כנתינה פולנייה. בתה שווה נישאה שם ב-1941, נישואין שהארכיון הזה כבר החזיק מבלי לראות מה עומד מאחוריהם. וכך, כשהגיעו דוד ולוסיה לבלגיה ב-1946, לא הייתה זו ארץ שהמשפחה מעולם לא דרכה בה: חלק ממנה חי שם לאורך כל הכיבוש, במרחק מאה קילומטרים מבריסל. האם הלך דוד למקום שבו היו לו אנשים — אין בידינו מסמך שאומר זאת. שווה לשאול, ולא שווה להמציא.
text.pl: Jedna rzecz o Belgii leżała na widoku. Ciotka Dawida, Jenta — siostra jego ojca — spędziła wojnę w Liège, przy Rue Lairesse 88, zarejestrowana jako obywatelka polska. Jej córka Szewa wyszła tam za mąż w 1941. Gdy więc Dawid i Łucja dotarli do Belgii w 1946, nie był to kraj, w którym rodzina nigdy nie była. Czy Dawid poszedł tam, gdzie miał swoich — żaden dokument tego nie mówi.
text.fr: Une chose au sujet de la Belgique était restée sous nos yeux. La tante de David, Jente — la sœur de son père — a passé la guerre à Liège, rue Lairesse 88, enregistrée comme ressortissante polonaise. Sa fille Szewa s'y est mariée en 1941. Ainsi, quand David et Lusia sont arrivés en Belgique en 1946, ce n'était pas un pays où la famille n'avait jamais mis les pieds. Aucun document en notre possession ne dit si David est allé là où il avait des siens.

sources: Wartime name record 4494611 (Jenta Rapaport, Rue Lairesse 88, Liège)
Liège marriage of Szewa Horowitz and Markus Türkel, 1941

title.en: Sète, the Theodor Herzl, Cyprus
title.pl: Sète, Theodor Herzl, Cypr
title.fr: Sète, le Theodor Herzl, Chypre

text.en: On 2 April 1947 David and Shimon sailed from Sète in southern France aboard the Theodor Herzl — the ex-British cable-layer HMS Guardian, built at Newcastle in 1907, carrying 2,641 ma'apilim gathered from camps across France and Belgium. Shimon was nine. Lusia stayed behind in Brussels with the seven-month-old Dov.
text.he: ב-2 באפריל 1947 הפליגו דוד ושמעון מסֶט שבדרום צרפת באונייה ״תיאודור הרצל״ — ספינת הכבלים הבריטית לשעבר HMS Guardian, שנבנתה בניוקאסל ב-1907, ונשאה 2,641 מעפילים ממחנות ברחבי צרפת ובלגיה. שמעון היה בן תשע. לוסיה נשארה בבריסל עם דב בן שבעת החודשים.
text.pl: 2 kwietnia 1947 Dawid i Szymon wypłynęli z Sète na południu Francji na pokładzie Theodora Herzla — dawnego brytyjskiego kablowca HMS Guardian, zbudowanego w Newcastle w 1907, wiozącego 2641 ma’apilim zebranych z obozów we Francji i Belgii. Szymon miał dziewięć lat. Łucja została w Brukseli z siedmiomiesięcznym Dovem.
text.fr: Le 2 avril 1947, David et Shimon quittèrent Sète, dans le sud de la France, à bord du Theodor Herzl — l’ancien câblier britannique HMS Guardian, construit à Newcastle en 1907, transportant 2 641 ma’apilim rassemblés dans les camps de France et de Belgique. Shimon avait neuf ans. Lusia resta à Bruxelles avec Dov, âgé de sept mois.

sources: Palyam / ship histories — the vessel is fully documented

text.en: On 13 April the Royal Navy boarded her off the coast. The passengers fought; three were killed and twenty-seven wounded. Everyone aboard was deported to Cyprus, and David and Shimon were interned at Karaolos, north of Famagusta, for about eight months. The camps there held 53,510 Jews behind wire between 1946 and 1949, and some two thousand children were born inside them. Shimon was released from Atlit in 1948.
text.he: ב-13 באפריל השתלט עליה הצי המלכותי מול החוף. הנוסעים נלחמו; שלושה נהרגו ועשרים ושבעה נפצעו. כל מי שהיה על הסיפון גורש לקפריסין, ודוד ושמעון נעצרו בקרַאוֹלוֹס, מצפון לפמגוסטה, כשמונה חודשים. המחנות שם החזיקו 53,510 יהודים מאחורי גדרות בין 1946 ל-1949, וכאלפיים ילדים נולדו בתוכם. שמעון שוחרר מעתלית ב-1948.
text.pl: 13 kwietnia Royal Navy wzięła statek abordażem u wybrzeży. Pasażerowie stawili opór; trzech zginęło, dwudziestu siedmiu zostało rannych. Wszystkich deportowano na Cypr, a Dawida i Szymona internowano w Karaolos na północ od Famagusty na jakieś osiem miesięcy. Tamtejsze obozy przetrzymywały za drutami 53 510 Żydów w latach 1946–1949, a wewnątrz urodziło się około dwóch tysięcy dzieci. Szymon został zwolniony z Atlit w 1948.
text.fr: Le 13 avril, la Royal Navy l’arraisonna au large. Les passagers résistèrent ; trois furent tués et vingt-sept blessés. Tous furent déportés à Chypre, et David et Shimon furent internés à Karaolos, au nord de Famagouste, pendant environ huit mois. Ces camps retinrent 53 510 Juifs derrière les barbelés entre 1946 et 1949, et quelque deux mille enfants y naquirent. Shimon fut libéré d’Atlit en 1948.

title.en: Haifa
title.pl: Hajfa
title.fr: Haïfa

text.en: Lusia sailed from Brussels with Dov on the Kadima. She had waited more than a year alone with the baby, working, while David and Shimon were behind wire. The Haifa burial register records her year of immigration as 1948 and David's as 1946 — the two-year gap the memoir describes, written into their own graves. Dov's first journey was with his mother, the two of them.
text.he: לוסיה הפליגה מבריסל עם דב באונייה ״קדימה״. היא המתינה יותר משנה לבדה עם התינוק, ועבדה, בזמן שדוד ושמעון היו מאחורי גדרות. פנקס הקבורה בחיפה רושם את שנת עלייתה 1948 ואת של דוד 1946 — פער השנתיים שהיומן מתאר, חקוק ברשומות קבריהם שלהם. מסעו הראשון של דב היה עם אמו, שניהם לבדם.
text.pl: Łucja wypłynęła z Brukseli z Dovem na statku Kadima. Czekała ponad rok sama z niemowlęciem, pracując, gdy Dawid i Szymon byli za drutami. Rejestr pochówków w Hajfie zapisuje rok jej alii jako 1948, a Dawida jako 1946 — dwuletnia luka, którą opisuje pamiętnik, wpisana w ich własne groby. Pierwsza podróż Dova była z matką, we dwoje.
text.fr: Lusia quitta Bruxelles avec Dov à bord du Kadima. Elle avait attendu plus d’un an, seule avec le bébé, en travaillant, pendant que David et Shimon étaient derrière les barbelés. Le registre funéraire de Haïfa note son année d’immigration : 1948, et celle de David : 1946 — l’écart de deux ans que décrit le mémoire, inscrit dans leurs propres tombes. Le premier voyage de Dov fut avec sa mère, tous les deux.

text.en: In Haifa she saw her parents for the first time since 1933. The family settled on Abbas Street, and later bought an apartment on Moriah Street with German reparations — money David argued with himself about taking. He worked as a customs broker, the trade his son Dov followed, and then his grandson Doron.
text.he: בחיפה ראתה את הוריה לראשונה מאז 1933. המשפחה התיישבה ברחוב עבאס, ולימים קנתה דירה ברחוב מוריה בכספי הפיצויים מגרמניה — כסף שדוד התלבט אם לקחת. הוא עבד כעמיל מכס, המקצוע שבו הלך בנו דב, ואחריו נכדו דורון.
text.pl: W Hajfie zobaczyła rodziców po raz pierwszy od 1933. Rodzina zamieszkała przy ulicy Abbas, a później kupiła mieszkanie przy ulicy Moria za niemieckie odszkodowania — pieniądze, o które Dawid spierał się sam ze sobą. Pracował jako agent celny; ten zawód przejął jego syn Dov, a potem wnuk Doron.
text.fr: À Haïfa, elle revit ses parents pour la première fois depuis 1933. La famille s’installa rue Abbas, puis acheta un appartement rue Moriah avec les réparations allemandes — un argent que David hésita longtemps à accepter. Il fut commissionnaire en douane, métier que suivirent son fils Dov, puis son petit-fils Doron.

text.en: In 1986 a granddaughter, Hadas, asked her teacher Esther Weiss for help with a school assignment, and Esther sat down and interviewed Lusia. Ninety pages in Hebrew. Without them, almost nothing in this archive between 1939 and 1948 would have a voice at all.
text.he: ב-1986 ביקשה נכדה, הדס, עזרה ממורתה אסתר ויס במטלת בית ספר, ואסתר ישבה וראיינה את לוסיה. תשעים עמודים בעברית. בלעדיהם, כמעט דבר בארכיון הזה בין 1939 ל-1948 לא היה נשמע כלל.
text.pl: W 1986 wnuczka, Hadas, poprosiła swoją nauczycielkę Esther Weiss o pomoc w szkolnym zadaniu, a Esther usiadła i przeprowadziła z Łucją rozmowy. Dziewięćdziesiąt stron po hebrajsku. Bez nich prawie nic w tym archiwum między 1939 a 1948 nie miałoby głosu.
text.fr: En 1986, une petite-fille, Hadas, demanda de l’aide à son professeur Esther Weiss pour un devoir scolaire, et Esther s’assit et interrogea Lusia. Quatre-vingt-dix pages en hébreu. Sans elles, presque rien dans ces archives entre 1939 et 1948 n’aurait de voix.

text.en: David died on 29 August 1990 and Lusia on 28 December 1996. They are buried beside one another at Sde Yehoshua, graves 102ד and 102ג. Her burial record names her father Eliyahu and her mother Matilda — the same two people her memoir opens with, sixty years earlier and in another language. The last page of the record matches the first page of the testimony.
text.he: דוד נפטר ב-29 באוגוסט 1990 ולוסיה ב-28 בדצמבר 1996. הם טמונים זה לצד זו בשדה יהושע, קברים 102ד ו-102ג. רשומת הקבורה שלה נוקבת באביה אליהו ובאמה מטילדה — אותם שני אנשים שבהם נפתח יומנה, שישים שנה קודם ובשפה אחרת. העמוד האחרון של הרשומה תואם לעמוד הראשון של העדות.
text.pl: Dawid zmarł 29 sierpnia 1990, Łucja 28 grudnia 1996. Spoczywają obok siebie na cmentarzu Sde Jehoszua, groby 102ד i 102ג. Jej akt pochówku wymienia ojca Eliahu i matkę Matyldę — tych samych dwoje ludzi, od których zaczyna się jej pamiętnik, sześćdziesiąt lat wcześniej i w innym języku. Ostatnia strona dokumentu zgadza się z pierwszą stroną świadectwa.
text.fr: David mourut le 29 août 1990 et Lusia le 28 décembre 1996. Ils reposent l’un à côté de l’autre à Sde Yehoshua, tombes 102ד et 102ג. Son acte d’inhumation nomme son père Eliyahu et sa mère Matilda — les deux mêmes personnes par lesquelles s’ouvre son mémoire, soixante ans plus tôt et dans une autre langue. La dernière page du registre correspond à la première page du témoignage.

title.pl: Powrót
title.fr: Le retour

text.en: In April 2015 Dov flew to Poland with his son Doron. They spent a week in Warsaw — the Old Town, the Barbican, the Royal Castle, a city flattened and put back stone by stone — and on 19 April they drove to Przemyśl. That is not a sightseeing stop. Przemyśl is the town where Berish and Rebeka were living when the war came; it is the residence the Auschwitz death books give for Berish, and it is where Lusia’s memoir says the Germans killed one of David’s parents on a fabricated charge. Most of the forty photographs from that day are taken through a car windscreen, driving its streets slowly, in the rain.
text.he: באפריל 2015 טס דב לפולין עם בנו דורון. הם עשו שבוע בוורשה — העיר העתיקה, הברבקן, הטירה המלכותית, עיר שנמחקה ונבנתה מחדש אבן אחר אבן — וב-19 באפריל נסעו לפשמישל. זו אינה עצירת תיירים. פשמישל היא העיירה שבה חיו בעריש ורבקה עם פרוץ המלחמה; זו כתובת המגורים שנוקבים בה ספרי המתים של אושוויץ עבור בעריש, וזה המקום שבו, לפי ספר הזיכרונות של לוסיה, הרגו הגרמנים את אחד מהוריו של דוד באשמת שווא. רוב ארבעים התצלומים מאותו יום צולמו מבעד לשמשת מכונית, בנסיעה איטית ברחובותיה, בגשם.
text.pl: W kwietniu 2015 Dow polechiał do Polski z synem Doronem. Tydzień w Warszawie — Stare Miasto, Barbakan, Zamek Królewski — a 19 kwietnia pojechali do Przemyśla. To nie przystanek turystyczny: w Przemyślu mieszkali Berisz i Rebeka, gdy przyszła wojna, i to Przemyśl podają jako jego miejsce zamieszkania obozowe księgi zgonów. Większość czterdziestu zdjęć z tego dnia zrobiono przez przednią szybę samochodu.
text.fr: En avril 2015, Dov s’est rendu en Pologne avec son fils Doron. Une semaine à Varsovie — la vieille ville, la Barbacane, le Château royal — puis, le 19 avril, la route de Przemyśl. Ce n’est pas une étape touristique : c’est la ville où vivaient Berish et Rebeka quand la guerre est venue, celle que les registres de décès d’Auschwitz donnent comme résidence de Berish. La plupart des quarante photographies de ce jour-là sont prises à travers un pare-brise.

sources: Dov and Doron, Warsaw and Przemyśl albums, April 2015

text.en: In June 2018 he went to Brussels, where he was born on 28 August 1946 — four months after his father filled in a Displaced Persons card in that city and wrote "Palestine or U.S.A." in the box for where he wanted to go. In January 2019 he went to Katowice, in the snow, and photographed it from above and on foot: the town of the separation nobody recorded, where the family was together before David and Shimon went one way and Lusia and the baby another. One hundred and twenty photographs from the four journeys are in this archive.
text.he: ביוני 2018 נסע לבריסל, שבה נולד ב-28 באוגוסט 1946 — ארבעה חודשים אחרי שאביו מילא באותה עיר כרטיס עקורים ורשם במשבצת היעד ״פלשתינה או ארה״ב״. בינואר 2019 נסע לקטוביץ, בשלג, וצילם אותה מלמעלה וברגל: עיירת ההיפרדות שאיש לא תיעד, שבה הייתה המשפחה יחד לפני שדוד ושמעון פנו לדרך אחת ולוסיה והתינוק לאחרת. מאה ועשרים תצלומים מארבעת המסעות שמורים בארכיון הזה.
text.pl: W czerwcu 2018 pojechał do Brukseli, gdzie urodził się 28 sierpnia 1946 — cztery miesiące po tym, jak jego ojciec wypełnił w tym mieście kartę dipisa i wpisał „Palestyna albo USA”. W styczniu 2019 pojechał do Katowic, w śniegu. Sto dwadzieścia zdjęć z czterech podróży jest w tym archiwum.
text.fr: En juin 2018, il est allé à Bruxelles, où il est né le 28 août 1946 — quatre mois après que son père y a rempli une fiche de personne déplacée en inscrivant « Palestine ou U.S.A. ». En janvier 2019, il est allé à Katowice, sous la neige. Cent vingt photographies de ces quatre voyages sont dans ces archives.

sources: Dov and Doron, Brussels and Katowice albums, 2018 and 2019

text.en: It is worth saying what that means for an archive like this one. Every other chapter here is assembled from what other people wrote down — clerks, registrars, a camp administration, a memoir. This is the only chapter in which somebody in the story goes back and looks for himself, and the pictures are his. Nothing in them was recovered. They were made.
text.he: כדאי לומר מה משמעות הדבר עבור ארכיון כמו זה. כל פרק אחר כאן מורכב ממה שאנשים אחרים רשמו — פקידים, רשמי מרשם, מנהלת מחנה, ספר זיכרונות. זהו הפרק היחיד שבו מישהו מן הסיפור חוזר ומביט בעצמו, והתמונות הן שלו. שום דבר בהן לא אוחזר. הן נעשו.
text.pl: Warto powiedzieć, co to znaczy dla takiego archiwum. Każdy inny rozdział złożony jest z tego, co zapisali inni — urzędnicy, administracja obozu, pamiętnik. To jedyny rozdział, w którym ktoś z tej historii wraca i patrzy sam, a zdjęcia są jego. Nic w nich nie zostało odzyskane. Zostały zrobione.
text.fr: Il vaut la peine de dire ce que cela signifie pour de telles archives. Tous les autres chapitres sont assemblés à partir de ce que d’autres ont écrit — des employés, une administration de camp, un mémoire. C’est le seul chapitre où quelqu’un de l’histoire revient et regarde lui-même, et les images sont les siennes. Rien n’y a été retrouvé. Elles ont été faites.

documents.summary_en: Lusia (Leah) Rapaport née Weitzner's memoir, dictated and compiled in 1986 by her granddaughter's teacher Esther Weiss. The primary historical document for Lusia's life from childhood in Bolechów through marriage in Muszyna (Feb 1938), survival under Nazi occupation in Lwów with false identities, escape with David and Shimon, post-war Brussels and the journey to Israel. Settled in Haifa, Moriah Street 93. OCR'd 2026-05-20 via Google Cloud Vision (~70k Hebrew chars). Translated to English and Polish by Claude Haiku 4.5 (batched). PRIMARY SOURCE for resolving H1 Mosina = Muszyna, and confirming David's wooden-wagon escape, Lota's existence, the Legionów 24 address, and the marriage date Feb 1938.

documents.summary_en: IPN academic paper covering Soviet repressions in the border zone with Germany 1939-1941. Includes a detailed section on 'Passportization' — the forced Soviet passport campaign that all residents of border towns like Przemyśl had to navigate. Basia shared this paper as historical CONTEXT — Leah was briefly in Soviet-occupied Przemyśl in 1939, and this paper documents what life under that occupation looked like for everyone living there. The paper also informs a planned formal IPN application for any Rapaport family records held by the Polish Institute of National Remembrance (see h_ipn_application). Reading this paper helps the family understand the conditions David and Leah lived through — both Soviet and Nazi occupations — before they were able to escape and reach Brussels in 1946.

documents.summary_en: This record was closed on 25 May 2026 as belonging to a different man, and its people were removed. That verdict rested on the second file in it — a Tarnów birth register page recording a Benzion Rapaport born 6 August 1884 to Mojżesz Rapaport and Regina Schiff. That page is indeed someone else. But it is not this certificate. The certificate, read in full from Basia’s own scan on 6 August 2026, says: applicant Rapaport Berisch; father Mojżesz Saul; origin Tarnów, Folwarczna 9; present address Stanisławów, Kościuszki 4; and, under children aged fourteen and under, „Mendel 12 lat, Lotte 8 lat”. David Mendel was twelve in July 1924 and Lota was eight. Basia has now filed this certificate inside our Berish’s own folder. Four things point one way — the father’s name, the Stanisławów address the archive already held for him, the two children by name and age, and a date one month before his August 1924 passport application. The 1884 Tarnów birth entry points the other way and stays on the record. The question is open again rather than settled the other way, and it is one for Basia.

documents.summary_en: Zygmunt Griffel was David Memek's first cousin once removed — son of Dawid Mendel Griffel Sr. (Rebeka's brother, Leizor Griffel's eldest son). This page establishes him as a major Galician-Jewish timber industrialist in 1934-35: 60,000 t/year to England, a five-port operation, with ambitions to brand Polish softwood. The 1938 Muszyna sawmill operating under 'Segal-Żupnik-Wilf' (per Rafał Żebrowski's Holocaust article) is identified in 1938 Przegląd Drzewny as a Zygmunt Griffel front company. Lusia's Muszyna hotel Willa Helin was in Zygmunt's sawmill town — the family-business ecosystem extended from Lwów-Gdynia exports down to Carpathian spa-town milling.

documents.summary_en: Primary documentary confirmation of Berisz's parents (Moshe + Menukha) and Holocaust fate (Auschwitz). PoT year of birth (1888) differs from passport application (1886) — the passport is a contemporary primary document and is the more reliable source for date. WHO FILED IT. The declaration at the foot gives a filer living in Haifa, at a street only partly legible with house number 93, signing on 26 April 1953. Where the form asks what the filer was to the person, the word written is בנו — his son. The signature reads רפפורט ד. The identification does not rest on that signature: Berish and Rebeka had one son, David, their other child being Lota, so "his son" is David whoever wrote the letters. He filed it seven years after reaching the country, for parents he had last seen before the war. Yad Vashem’s own database would show the submitter independently; it refused connection from this machine on 11 August 2026, so that confirmation is still outstanding.

title.pl: Rekord ofiary Muzeum Auschwitz — Bernard Rapaport #188161

documents.summary_en: The museum page itself, received from Basia on 6 August 2026. It closes a gap this record had left open in its own words. Birth date and birthplace match our Berish exactly — 30 July 1886, Radomyśl Wielki. He was given prisoner number 27310, arrived at the camp on 27 March 1942 and died there on 29 March 1942. Two days. His occupation is entered as robotnik, labourer; he was an industrialist in Stanisławów, and the word is the camp’s, not his. The family’s 1953 Yad Vashem testimony says 1940 — written eleven years later and two years out. Both are kept; the register is nearer.

documents.summary_en: ⚠ NOT OUR FAMILY (most likely). This certificate of divorce, issued 16 September 1941 in Petach Tikvah, Mandatory Palestine, dissolves the marriage of Lea bat Shimon HaKohen Rapaport (age 29) and Michael Sigal (age 29, baker). Lea's father is named Shimon HaKohen Rapaport — but our paternal-line Shimon was a Griffel ancestor, not a Rapaport, and our Lusia (Lea Weitzner-Rapaport) was hiding in Lwów under the alias 'Maria Cizlik' in 1941. This Lea Rapaport (b. ~1912) is therefore a different person, from a different Rapaport-HaKohen rabbinical branch. The CC-Cohen patronymic suggests she may still be a distant cousin within the broader Rapoport-Kohen rabbinical dynasty, but no proximate link to our family has been established.

title.en: Application for Palestinian Citizenship — Hirsch Herman Nussbaum and Inge née Rosenbusch, Haifa 1945 (31 pages)
title.he: בקשה לאזרחות פלשתינאית (א״י) — הירש הרמן נוסבאום ואינגה לבית רוזנבוש, חיפה 1945 (31 עמודים)
title.pl: Wniosek o obywatelstwo palestyńskie — Hirsch Herman Nussbaum i Inge z d. Rosenbusch, Hajfa 1945 (31 stron)
title.fr: Demande de citoyenneté palestinienne — Hirsch Herman Nussbaum et Inge née Rosenbusch, Haïfa 1945 (31 pages)

documents.summary_en:
Read page by page on 3 August 2026. It is a Government of Palestine, Department of Migration file: APPLICATION FOR PALESTINIAN CITIZENSHIP, headquarters serial 90563, held by the Israel State Archives (גנזך המדינה) in the Mandate Government series מ, file 3211/050.

APPLICANT: NUSSBAUM, Hirsch Herman. Wife: Inge, maiden name Rosenbusch.

What the file states:
  • Applicant's Polish passport no. 118839, issued at PRZEMYŚL on 21 September 1938
  • Wife's German passport no. 94, issued at BORKEN on 10 July 1935
  • First entry into Palestine: 12 October 1938; immigrant registration HA/5934/B of the same date
  • Wife and children registered HA/4302/A on 22 August 1938
  • Marriage solemnised at HAIFA on 12 June 1941 — Haifa Jewish Community Rabbinical Office certificate H-49343 of 15 June 1941
  • A son, MORDECHAI YOSEF, born at Haifa on 25 April 1943 — certificate 1591/43 of 14 May 1943
  • Fee of 250 mils, receipt 715052 of 29 October 1945; application made at Haifa
  • Approved 29 November 1945; naturalisation certificate no. 48628
  • Both passports withdrawn at Haifa in 1946

WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN. Our tree holds Zwi (Hirsch) Nussbaum, born in Przemyśl in 1919 — father of Yehudit Shlomit Ayalon, the living cousin found in June 2026, who is named after Freida, Berisz's sister. Zwi is Hirsch. A Polish passport issued at Przemyśl in September 1938 fits a nineteen-year-old from that town leaving for Palestine, and he entered three weeks later.

That is a strong lead and it is NOT a proof. The pages read so far carry no birth date and no parents' names for the applicant, which are what would settle it. The wife here is Inge Rosenbusch and the recorded child is a son, Mordechai Yosef; we do not know the name of Yehudit Shlomit's mother. Nussbaum is not a rare name. He is therefore NOT attached to any person in the tree until the particulars page is read.

NEXT: the remaining pages of the file almost certainly carry the applicant's declaration with date and place of birth and his father's name. Reading those decides it either way.

decoded_fields.identification: CONFIRMED as the file of Zwi (Hirsch) Ayalon Nussbaum: the children listed are Mordekhai Yosef and YEHUDIT SHLOMIT, and Yehudit Shlomit Ayalon is the living cousin who reconnected with this family in June 2026. Birth particulars declared: Tarnów, 6 May 1919 — which conflicts with the Przemyśl birth register (7 May 1919) and is recorded rather than resolved.
decoded_fields.address_1946: 24 Hillel Street, Haifa — written in English on the applicant’s own declaration. An earlier reading of "34" from the Hebrew notice of January 1946 was mine and is withdrawn; the English form is the clearer hand.
decoded_fields.certificate_numbers: RESOLVED by p.9. A minute of 27 August 1946 from the Commissioner for Migration and Statistics reads "cancel cert. and issue a new one", five days after the applicant signed the amended form adding Yehudit Shlomit. So the file holds two numbers because there were two certificates: 47589, issued at Jerusalem 25 January 1946 and shown on the certificate itself (p.19), and 48628, recorded on the summary sheet and the receipt note as the certificate issued. No reconciliation is invented here — the cancellation minute is on the page.
decoded_fields.passports_surrendered: Polish no. 118839 and wife’s German no. 94, surrendered at Haifa, 1946
decoded_fields.third_child_1946: RESOLVED. The "child born to applicant" reported by the Haifa Immigration Office on 14 May 1946 is YEHUDIT SHLOMIT herself, added by hand to the children’s table on the applicant’s own declaration (p.31): born at Haifa, April 1946. There is no third child. The applicant re-signed the amended form on 23 August 1946.
decoded_fields.wife_birth: Inge Rosenbusch, born Kassel, Germany, 3 July 1922; German nationality before marriage
decoded_fields.clerk_note: At the foot of the declaration: "1919 only acc. to ppt" — the clerk recording that the stated birth year rested on the passport alone. Relevant to the Tarnów/Przemyśl and 6/7 May conflict: the applicant may have been working from a passport rather than a certificate.
decoded_fields.supporters: Dr Gruber, physician, 15 Pevsner Street, Haifa; Dr Platner, pharmacist, Neveh Sha’anan — the two residents who vouched for the application
decoded_fields.photographs: Page 20 carries TWO MOUNTED PHOTOGRAPHS — Inge on the left, the applicant on the right. The form itself demanded them: "Three small photographs of applicant and of his wife if he is married should be furnished. Photomaton photographs will not be accepted." Both have been cropped out and attached to their person records. This is the only known photograph of Inge.
decoded_fields.yehudit_shlomit_birth: 25 April 1946 at Haifa — settled by the Ministry of the Interior confirmation of April 1996 bound into the file, which lists the wife and both children with places and dates. She and her brother share a birthday three years apart.
decoded_fields.ministry_confirmation_1996: State of Israel, Ministry of the Interior, Population Administration, Citizenship Department, ref 90563, dated 21 April 1996, signed Esther Migian, citizenship coordinator. It confirms the grant of Palestinian citizenship and lists those included: Inge (Kassel, Germany, 3.7.1922) wife; Mordekhai Yosef (Haifa, 25.4.1943) son; Yehudit Shlomit (Haifa, 25.4.1946) daughter. Someone requested this confirmation in 1996 — the same year a reader’s slip in the file shows the original being pulled from the State Archives.
decoded_fields.oath_signed: Oath of allegiance signed "Herman Nussbaum", 19 December 1945 (p.7; p.28 is the blank duplicate)
decoded_fields.applicants_father: ELIAHU-MORDECHAI NUSSBAUM — written by Zwi himself in the father’s field of his 1996 Ministry of the Interior application (p.13). This archive had carried the man as "[unknown given name] Nussbaum, INFERRED" for a year.
decoded_fields.hebraised_surname: By 1996 the family used AYALON. The 1996 application is signed "AYALON (NUSSBAUM)" and the return label reads "Inge & Zwi Ayalon, 84 Sderot HaNassi, Haifa 34529".
decoded_fields.final_particulars_sheet: p.15 is the final amended particulars sheet: both photographs, and both children typed — Mordekhai Yosef 25.4.1943 and Yehudit Shlomit 25.4.1946.
decoded_fields.identity_number: The 1996 form carries his Israeli identity number. It is deliberately not reproduced in this archive.

title.en: Descendant chart of Abraham Abe Rapaport — Basia, 2026
title.he: תרשים צאצאי אברהם אבה רפפורט — בסיה, 2026
title.pl: Tablica potomków Abrahama Abe Rapaporta

documents.summary_en:
THE CHART THAT NAMED MOSES SAUL’S PARENTS. Read 5 August 2026. It descends from Abraham Abe Rapaport and carries document thumbnails above most cards, so Basia is working from registers rather than from other people’s trees.

The card that matters: SZABSE RAPAPORT, born 30 January 1823 at Tarnów, died 1884, married to ITA FEIGA JAHR (died before 1897). On the sibling bar beneath them sits MOSES SAUL RAPAPORT, born about 1858, died 8 November 1933 at Tarnów, married to MENYCHA LEINER.

Every particular matches what this archive already held independently — the Tarnów death record 1933/152 gives the same death date, the same age and the same two parents, and we had Menukha’s maiden name Leiner from the Sambor marriage record of 1913, which Basia did not use. The chart adds two things we never had: Ita Feiga’s maiden name, and Szabse’s date of birth.

Also on that sibling bar, so also children of Szabse and Ita Feiga: LIEBE (b. 28 March 1847), MAJER (b. about 1849, d. 22 October 1920, married Cerka/Cecylia Margulies) and IZCHAK CHAIM (d. 15 August 1921, Kraków). Moses Saul had brothers and sisters, and this archive did not know their names an hour earlier.

The chart reaches further back still — Herschl Rapaport, born about 1792 at Tarnów, died 23 May 1874 — and outward across Tarnów and Kraków. It has NOT yet been read line by line.

title.en: The Lurie Legacy — Descendants of the Shach, with Basia’s 2026 overlay
title.he: מורשת לוריא — צאצאי הש״ך, עם סימוני בסיה 2026

documents.summary_en:
Basia’s marks run our line up into a published rabbinical genealogy. Highlighted in pink and named on the sheet: MOSES SAUL, and IZCHAK MAJER CHAIM — the same brothers who stand beside Moses Saul on her own descendant chart. Above them she highlights SHABTAI, A.B.D. Dombrowa, died 1897, with an arrow to the Weidenfeld sheet; and higher still ABRAHAM ABALE, A.B.D. Tarnow, died 1872, the head of her chart. The ascent continues through Isaac Rappaport, A.B.D. Pinczow (1741-1774), to SHABTAI HaKOHEN — the SHaCH, 1621-1662 — and across to Saul WAHL and Israel KATZENELLENBOGEN.

HOW THIS ARCHIVE TREATS IT. The documented line stops at Szabse and Ita Feiga. Everything above them is a published compilation, and the Davidic descent at the top is TRADITION — held exactly as the Rapaport-Kohen priestly lineage is held: recorded, attributed, and never stated as proven descent. It is kept deliberately apart from the part we can put a record behind, so the documented part cannot be weakened by association if the traditional part is ever challenged.

NOTE THE CONFLICT: Rosenstein’s Shabtai died 1897, Basia’s own chart has Szabse dying 1884. See h_szabse_death_year.

title.en: The Lurie Legacy — the Weidenfeld family, with Basia’s 2026 overlay
title.he: מורשת לוריא — משפחת ויידנפלד, עם סימוני בסיה 2026

documents.summary_en:
Headed by SHABTAI RAPPAPORT, A.B.D. Dombrowa, died 1897 — the man Basia marks as our ancestor. Almost the whole descent below him is highlighted as confirmed against the Rapaport tree of 2026: his daughter Rachel (d. 1914), who married Jacob WEIDENFELD (1840-1894), A.B.D. Grzymalow, author of the responsa "Kochav MiYaakov"; Meir, A.B.D. Lukow (d. 1920); Isaac Haim, A.B.D. Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski (d. 1921), who married a daughter of Zeev Nachum BORNSTEIN — the card Basia labels MARGULESA; and onward to Nachum (1874-1939), the Chazon Nachum, A.B.D. Dombrowa, who "perished with his family", and to DovBerish of Trzebin (1881-1965), the Chebiner Rov.

If the identification holds, our paternal line runs into a dynasty of rabbinical court heads across Galicia — and into the Holocaust, repeatedly and by name. IT DEPENDS ENTIRELY on whether the 1897 Shabtai is the 1884 Szabse. Unresolved; see h_szabse_death_year.

title.en: Basia’s GEDCOM — the whole Rapaport tree as data, 5 August 2026
title.he: קובץ ה-GEDCOM של בסיה — אילן רפפורט כולו כנתונים, 5 באוגוסט 2026
title.pl: GEDCOM Basi — całe drzewo Rapaportów jako dane

documents.summary_en:
THE FILE THAT LETS THE TWO TREES BE COMPARED BY MACHINE. Read 5 August 2026.

1,442 individuals against our 179 — eight times the size. Birth years run from 1784, Abraham Abe Rapaport, to 1988. Surnames beyond Rapaport (196): Weidenfeld 35, Bornstein 34, Turkel 32, Schneerson 31, Horowitz 17 — the rabbinical connections the Rosenstein sheets pointed at are inside her tree, not just alongside it.

THE TREES AGREE. 36 people match on an EXACT birth date, and on every one of those the death dates agree too, except where one of us simply had nothing. Two independent research efforts, one from Polish registers and one from family papers and Israeli records, produced the same answers. That is the strongest validation this archive has had.

ALL FOUR PRINCIPALS ARE IN IT: Dawid Mendel b.25.12.1911 d.29.8.1990; Lea (Lusia) Weitzner (Wizner) b.8.4.1913 d.1996; Shimon b.22.6.1937; Dov b.28.8.1946.

WHAT WE GAINED IMMEDIATELY: Jechiel Turkel — Alte Leja’s husband — died 17 JULY 1942 AT AUSCHWITZ. We had no death date for him at all. Inge Nussbaum died at Jerusalem, 14 January 2009, born at Kassel. Plus two birthplaces.

WHAT IS STILL TO DO: she holds 52 Rapaports with full birth dates that we do not, and 24 Rapaports whose death falls between 1939 and 1945 — Tarnów, Radomyśl Wielki, Kraków, Łuków, Biała Podlaska, Pińczów, Oświęcim. That is the family in the Holocaust, named. Importing them is a decision, not a formality: her confidence is not automatically ours, and anything brought across should carry her as its source.

title.pl: Dawid w szkole — sprawozdania I Gimnazjum Państwowego w Stanisławowie, 1926 i 1927/28
title.fr: David à l’école — rapports annuels du Premier Gymnase d’État, Stanisławów, 1926 et 1927/28

documents.summary_en: Sprawozdanie Dyrekcji I. Gimnazjum Państwowego im. M. Romanowskiego w Stanisławowie za rok szkolny 1927/28 — the annual report of the First State Gymnasium named for Mieczysław Romanowski, printed in Stanisławów in 1928 by Leon Dankiewicz, the same printer whose name sits at the foot of Berish’s 1924 certificate. It marks the school’s bicentenary, 1728–1928. This is where David was a pupil: the family had been in Stanisławów since 1918 and lived at Kościuszki 4. One of the three files Basia sent is labelled nieukończone — unfinished — and the archive repeats that label rather than guessing what it refers to.

title.en: Auschwitz Sterbebücher (death books) 1941–1943 — Berisch Rapaport, died 29 March 1942
title.he: ספרי המתים של אושוויץ (Sterbebücher) 1941–1943 — בעריש רפפורט, נפטר ב-29 במרץ 1942
title.pl: Księgi zgonów Auschwitz (Sterbebücher) 1941–1943 — Berisch Rapaport, zmarł 29 marca 1942
title.fr: Sterbebücher d’Auschwitz (registres de décès) 1941-1943 — Berisch Rapaport, mort le 29 mars 1942

documents.summary_en: The camp’s own death books, kept for prisoners registered in Auschwitz between July 1941 and December 1943 — 46 partially preserved volumes, 65,280 names. Berisch Rapaport, born 30 July 1886 at Radomyśl Wielki, died 29 March 1942. This is a second and independent witness to the date the Museum victim page gives, and the two agree to the day. It also carries something the Museum page does not: residence PRZEMYŚL. Lusia’s memoir says David’s parents were in Przemyśl when the war came, and that the Germans killed one of them there on a fabricated accusation. The register, written by the men who ran the camp, puts him in the same town. A memoir written from memory decades later and a German clerk’s entry made at the time agree, and neither could have been copying the other.

decoded_fields.source_scope: 46 volumes, 65,280 registered prisoners who died 29 Jul 1941 – 31 Dec 1943

title.en: Jenta Rapaport registered at Rue Lairesse 88, Liège, during the war
title.he: ינטה רפפורט רשומה ברחוב לרס 88, ליֶאז׳, בימי המלחמה
title.pl: Jenta Rapaport zarejestrowana przy Rue Lairesse 88 w Liège podczas wojny
title.fr: Jenta Rapaport enregistrée rue Lairesse 88, Liège, pendant la guerre

documents.summary_en: Jente Rapaport — David’s aunt, sister of his father Berish — spent the war in Liège at Rue Lairesse 88, registered as a Polish national. Her daughter Szewa Horowitz married Markus Türkel in Liège in 1941, and the archive already holds that marriage. Together they change the shape of one thing: when David and Lusia reached Belgium in 1946, Belgium was not a country the family had never been to. Part of it had been living there through the occupation, in a city 100 km from Brussels. Whether the two facts are connected — whether David went where he had people — is not stated by any document here, and the archive does not assert it.

open_questions.en: Did David and Lusia know Jente and Szewa were in Liège when they came to Belgium in 1946? Nothing in hand says so either way.
open_questions.he: האם דוד ולוסיה ידעו שינטה ושווה נמצאות בליאז׳ כשהגיעו לבלגיה ב-1946? שום דבר שבידינו אינו אומר כך או אחרת.

title.en: Auschwitz transport 689 — 55 men from the prison in Tarnów, 27 March 1942
title.he: טרנספורט 689 לאושוויץ — 55 גברים מבית הכלא בטרנוב, 27 במרץ 1942
title.pl: Transport 689 do Auschwitz — 55 mężczyzn z więzienia w Tarnowie, 27 marca 1942
title.fr: Transport 689 vers Auschwitz — 55 hommes de la prison de Tarnów, 27 mars 1942

documents.summary_en: The transport that carried David’s father to Auschwitz, read from the Museum’s own database rather than from a copy. Fifty-five men from the prison in Tarnów, registered at Auschwitz on 27 March 1942 with numbers 27305 to 27359, sent by the Security Police (Sicherheitspolizei) and Security Service (Sicherheitsdienst) of the Kraków district. The Museum records that no documentation survives explaining the circumstances of the transport’s arrival and admission. Eighteen of the fifty-five were identified in the camp records as Jewish, and seventeen of those died at Auschwitz; at least forty-one of the fifty-five died there. Berish Rapaport held number 27310 — the sixth in the block — and died two days after arrival, on 29 March 1942. The detail that changes the story is where the transport started: the prison in Tarnów. The family came from Radomyśl Wielki, a short way from Tarnów, and their registered address in 1924 was Tarnów, Folwarczna 9. He was not taken from Przemyśl and sent east; he was held in the town his family belonged to.

title.en: Everyone named Rapaport in the Auschwitz victims database — 26 people, one of them ours
title.he: כל מי שנקרא רפפורט במסד נתוני הקורבנות של אושוויץ — 26 בני אדם, אחד מהם שלנו
title.pl: Wszyscy o nazwisku Rapaport w bazie ofiar Auschwitz — 26 osób, jedna z nich nasza
title.fr: Toutes les personnes nommées Rapaport dans la base des victimes d’Auschwitz — 26, dont une des nôtres

documents.summary_en: Twenty-six people named Rapaport appear in the Auschwitz-Birkenau Museum’s victims database. Exactly one is ours: Berisch, born 30 July 1886 at Radomyśl Wielki, prisoner 27310. The other twenty-five were born in Radom, Warsaw, Będzin, Lwów, Volove, Chocz, Karczowice, Oestringen, Podwołoczyska and Józefów, or have no birthplace recorded at all. Nothing connects them to this family except a surname that was common across Poland, and this archive has already been wrong once by reading a shared name as a shared line. They are listed here because they are worth listing — and kept out of the family’s own records for the same reason.

title.en: Jacob’s Griffel tree — David’s mother’s side, 390 people, received 10 August 2026
title.he: עץ גריפל של יעקב — צד אמו של דוד, 390 בני אדם, התקבל ב-10 באוגוסט 2026

title.fr: L’arbre Griffel de Jacob — le côté maternel de David, 390 personnes, 10 août 2026

documents.summary_en: A second family archive, and a different family. Not one of its 569 files appears in Basia’s Rapaport export — this is the GRIFFEL line, David’s mother’s people, the side of the house this archive had least on. Rebeka Griffel, of whom we held a name, a year and a death recorded only in Lusia’s memoir, appears here with her parents: Lajzor Griffel, born 26 March 1850 at Nadwórna, died 1918, and Sara Matel Chajes, born 5 March 1851, died 1940. She had twelve brothers and sisters. Where the two archives overlap they agree without having consulted each other: Berish born 1886 at Radomyśl Wielki and dead at Auschwitz in 1942; David born 1911 at Nadwórna and dead at Haifa in 1990; Lota born about 1915. Jacob dates Rebeka’s death "1942?" — with the question mark — which sits beside our 1942 and the 1943 on her Yad Vashem page. All three are kept.

title.en: Yad Vashem Page of Testimony 53075 — Lotte Schmid-Rapaport, filed by her brother David, 26 April 1953
title.he: דף עד ביד ושם 53075 — לוטה שמיד־רפפורט, הוגש בידי אחיה דוד, 26 באפריל 1953
title.pl: Karta Świadectwa Yad Vashem 53075 — Lotte Schmid-Rapaport, złożona przez brata Dawida, 26 kwietnia 1953
title.fr: Feuille de Témoignage Yad Vashem 53075 — Lotte Schmid-Rapaport, déposée par son frère David, 26 avril 1953

documents.summary_en: The third form David filled in that day. His sister Lotte was born in Vienna in 1914 — this page says 1914, the family trees say 27 September 1915, and both are kept — daughter of Berish and Rebeka, married, a Polish national in 1939, and she died at Lwów. This archive held no death for her at all: she was a birth record from Vienna and then nothing. Her brother, writing in Haifa eight years after the war, put down where she died and signed himself אחיה, her brother. He did not fill in the year. The married name on the page, Schmid, is new here too — nothing else in this archive records that she married, or whom. CROSS-CHECKED 11 August 2026 against both family archives. Basia holds her as Charlotta Rapaport, born 27 September 1915 in Vienna, married to "… Szmid" — the surname without a given name — and records NO death. Jacob holds her as Lota Rapaport, born about 1915, with no marriage and no death. So the married name is confirmed twice over and the place of death is confirmed nowhere else: this page is the only statement about her fate in any of the three archives. Note also that Basia’s tree contains a first cousin, Charlotte Horowitz, born 21 November 1914 in Vienna to Berish’s sister Jente — same name, same city, one year apart. The 1914 on this page matches the cousin; the parents on this page, בעריש and רבקה, do not. The parents decide it.

title.en: What is in this archive, and what is not — coverage audit, 11 August 2026
title.he: מה יש בארכיון הזה ומה אין — ביקורת כיסוי, 11 באוגוסט 2026
title.pl: Co jest w tym archiwum, a czego nie ma — audyt kompletności, 11 sierpnia 2026
title.fr: Ce que contiennent ces archives, et ce qui manque — audit de couverture, 11 août 2026

documents.summary_en: Every source the family has given us has been walked file by file and compared against what this site actually serves — in both directions, because either one alone lies. Nothing the site references is missing, and nothing we were given is unpublished, with exactly two exceptions, both named: Photobook2.pdf, whose 47 pages are already here one by one, and "Lea and Shimon .pdf", which has never reached us. Along the way this audit found 71 files that every earlier pass had skipped in silence — all of them PDFs, because each publisher filtered on image extensions and said nothing about what it dropped. Among them a 1938 document from Rebeka Griffel’s own folder and a 1942 list from the Bolechów Holzwerke, the town where Lusia was born. That is why the audit walks the sources and not the site: a check that only asks "does everything here work" cannot see what never arrived.

title.en: Dov’s journeys back — Warsaw, Przemyśl, Brussels, Katowice (2015–2019)
title.he: מסעותיו של דב אל המקומות — ורשה, פשמישל, בריסל, קטוביץ (2015–2019)
title.pl: Podróże Dowa — Warszawa, Przemyśl, Bruksela, Katowice (2015–2019)
title.fr: Les retours de Dov — Varsovie, Przemyśl, Bruxelles, Katowice (2015-2019)

documents.summary_en: Four albums, 121 frames, 120 published. They are not holidays. Przemyśl is where Berish and Rebeka were when the war came — the camp register gives it as Berish’s residence, and the memoir says the Germans killed one of his parents there. Brussels is where Dov was born in 1946. Katowice is the town of the separation in chapter 5. Warsaw is the city that was flattened and rebuilt. Dov walked and drove them with his son and photographed what he saw. Every frame was looked at before publishing; one was left out, a hotel lavatory, and saying which is part of the check.

title.en: Lusia’s own Displaced Persons card, Brussels, 26 December 1945
title.he: כרטיס העקורים של לוסיה עצמה, בריסל, 26 בדצמבר 1945
title.pl: Karta dipisa Łucji, Bruksela, 26 grudnia 1945
title.fr: Fiche de personne déplacée de Lusia, Bruxelles, 26 décembre 1945

documents.summary_en: Lusia’s own card, the twin of David’s. She registered in Brussels on 26 December 1945 — three and a half months BEFORE he did on 9 April 1946, and eight months before Dov was born there. She signed it Rapaport Lea while the clerk filed her under her maiden name and added "ép.se Rapaport" at the top. Three things it gives us. Her parents: father Elias, mother’s maiden name MATHILDE WEINREB — the Weitzner–Weinreb line. The remark "Vient de Prague" — she came from a camp in Prague, which nothing else in this archive mentions and which is now an open question. And a birthplace that is simply wrong: HAIFA, PALESTINE. She was born in Bolechów. David’s card of the same series gives Cieszyn, also wrong. Two cards, two wrong birthplaces — and on Lusia’s the desired destination is Palestine. The archive records the pattern and asserts no motive.

documents.summary_en: Two days after she registered as a displaced person, a Jewish aid society asked the Belgian authorities to let her stay six months. It repeats the two strange things from her card — born Haifa, came from a camp in Prague — and adds an address: 250 rue des Coteaux, Schaerbeek. That is where Lusia was living in Brussels, and where she was still living when Dov was born eight months later.

Three months at a time, twice renewable. Dov was born under this arrangement.

Edward, born in Nadwórna, thirty-eight years old, an exporter, crossed into the United States from Montreal on 26 May 1941 to reside permanently, giving his father David Griffel at Kolomyja as his nearest relative in the country he came from. Doron reports that Basia has now finished the Weitzner side and found many of them emigrated to the United States, settling mainly in New Jersey; this card is the same movement on the Griffel side, and it is dated eight months before the family in Galicia was destroyed.

documents.summary_en: Nineteen years before the century turned violent, a man walked into a notary’s office in Tarnów and paid two crowns so that his wife could pick up his mail. The clerk wrote entry 392: Mojżesz Rapaport, capitalist in Tarnów, legalises his signature on a power of attorney for his wife Menicha to receive postal items. That is the whole document, and it is worth more than its size. This is Moses Saul Rapaport, born 1858, died in Tarnów on 8 November 1933 — David’s grandfather, Dov’s great-grandfather — and the tree records his occupation as "merchant"; the notary wrote "capitalist". And it is the only document this archive holds that names his wife at all: Menycha Leiner has, until today, been a name on a tree with no birth date, no death date and no paper of her own. Here she is, in 1904, being given legal authority over the family post.

title.en: Typed list of fifteen families, addressed care of Jakob Griffel in Bucharest — identified by the Pilecki Institute as belonging to the wartime operation to issue foreign passports to Jews
title.he: רשימה מודפסת של חמש-עשרה משפחות, ממוענת לידי יעקב גריפל בבוקרשט — מכון פילצקי זיהה אותה כשייכת למבצע הנפקת הדרכונים הזרים ליהודים בימי המלחמה

title.fr: Liste dactylographiée de quinze familles, adressée aux bons soins de Jakob Griffel à Bucarest — rattachée par l’Institut Pilecki à l’opération des passeports étrangers

documents.summary_en:
A torn sheet of typing that this archive misfiled for ten days as a portrait of Dr Jacob Griffel, because the file was named after him. It is not a portrait. It is a list of fifteen families — names, birth dates, street addresses in Kraków, Sosnowiec, Bielsko and Lublin — with his own forwarding address pencilled at the foot: care of Ing. L. Filderman, Strada Paleologu, Bucharest. Jacob Griffel was the Agudath Israel and Vaad Hatzalah rescue man in Istanbul. Shown this sheet, Ms Manowska of the Pilecki Institute — who researches the "passports of life" — recognised at sight that it came from the operation that issued foreign passports to Jews, and asked immediately where it had been found and what its reference number was.

Six of the fifteen entries are the children of Isaac Chaim Griffel and Judith Breit, and the birth dates match this family’s tree to the month: Dawid Mendel b. 1902 with his wife Laja and their daughter Rebeka Rachela; Schalom b. 1904 with his wife and two little girls; Samuel b. 1913; Amalia b. 1912; Rebeka b. July 1919; Osias Heinrich b. 1910. Entry 15 is their sister Teofila with her husband Rosenbojm and their small son. This was a man in Bucharest trying to get his own family onto paper that might save them.

And then the outcome, which the film must not soften. Samuel lived, and died in Brooklyn in 1999. Osias Heinrich lived, and died in Jersey City in 1968. Menashe Karmel, entry 6, lived until 1989. Schalom, his wife and both daughters were murdered in 1942. Schmul Rosenbojm was murdered in Lublin in 1942 and his son Izajasz in 1943. Zalman Horowitz died in 1945. Whether any passport was ever issued against this sheet, and whether it reached anybody, this archive cannot say.

title.en: Who held the child — four pages of the Dąbrowa Tarnowska birth register that date the death of Rabbi Szabse Rapaport
title.he: מי החזיק את התינוק — ארבעה עמודים מפנקס הלידות של דומברובה טרנובסקה המתארכים את פטירתו של הרב שבסה רפפורט
title.pl: Kto trzymał dziecko — cztery karty księgi urodzeń Dąbrowy Tarnowskiej, które datują śmierć rabina Szabsego Rapaporta
title.fr: Qui tenait l’enfant — quatre pages du registre des naissances de Dąbrowa Tarnowska qui datent la mort du rabbin Szabse Rapaport

documents.summary_en:
A rabbi’s death date, recovered without a death record — by watching who holds the babies.

A sandek is the man who holds the child at a circumcision, and the register names him every time. In Dąbrowa Tarnowska that man is Szabse Rapaport, rabbi of the town — until 27 April 1884, which is the last time his name appears. Three weeks later, on 19 May 1884, the sandek is Majer Rapaport, rabbi of Łuków — his son, standing in. From 26 September 1884 the office belongs to rabbi Hirsz Weiss, and it stays his for thirteen years. Then on 4 November 1897 the sandek in Dąbrowa is Nuchim Weidenfeld — Szabse’s grandson.

The page in the middle is the one to look at. On 15 June 1886, two years after the old rabbi had gone, the clerk copying the birth book wrote "Szabsa Rapaport, rabin w Dąbrowie" in the sandek column out of pure habit, and then squeezed "Hersz Weiss." into the gap above it. The correction is small and apologetic and it is still there, 140 years later.

And the custom seals it: Ashkenazi Jews name a child for the dead, never for the living. Three grandsons were named Schabse in the years straight after — June 1885, August 1885, July 1891 — each the first boy born in his branch. One of them, born 8 August 1885, was the son of Moses Saul and Menycha, which puts this argument inside our own line.

Basia’s conclusion: Rabbi Szabse Rapaport died in May 1884, and the 1897 date carried by the published rabbinical genealogies is the year the post passed from Weiss to Weidenfeld. It is as if Hirsz Weiss, who was rabbi of Dąbrowa for thirteen years, had been quietly removed from the tradition.

Column 8: "Sandek — MAJER RAPAPORT, rabin z Łukowa w Królestwie Polskim". Szabse’s own son, the rabbi of Łuków in Russian Poland, standing in — three weeks after his father’s last appearance.

In the sandek cell the clerk wrote "Szabsa Rapaport, rabin w Dąbrowie" — and then squeezed "Hersz Weiss." in above it, small, in the gap under the word Sandek. decoded_fields.the_naming_argument: Ashkenazi custom names a child for a dead ancestor, never a living one. Three grandsons were named Schabse immediately after: 15 June 1885, son of Izchak Chaim (extended_tree I517); 8 August 1885, son of Moses Saul (I949 — our own line); 2 July 1891, son of Majer (I135). In each case the first male descendant born after the death.
decoded_fields.what_the_1897_date_actually_is: The year Hirsz Weiss’s tenure ended and Nuchim Weidenfeld’s began. Basia’s reading: the tradition dropped Weiss entirely and slid Szabse’s death forward to the handover.

documents.summary_en: Stated by Basia on 20 August 2026, and it changes how every board she has sent should be read: on the Rosenstein sheets she marks in pink ONLY the elements that match the records she has verified. So she did not mark Shabtai’s death date — she left the 1897 out on purpose, because she does not accept it. An unmarked element on one of her boards is not something she overlooked. It is something she is declining to confirm.

title.pl: Grifflowie w prasie galicyjskiej, 1866-1946 — 128 stron, 142 notatki
title.fr: Les Griffel dans la presse galicienne, 1866-1946 — 128 pages, 142 notices

documents.summary_en: Basia wrote that while researching Muszyna she came across an unprecedented number of press sources, and that the local papers described the Griffels’ ups and downs much as papers describe celebrities now — so that in the articles you can catch glimpses of their personalities, which is rare. She is right. Eighty years of them: Taube Griffel’s spice, haberdashery and iron shop at Nadwórna registered in 1882 with power of attorney to her son Leizor; the credit cooperative of 1890; Leizor on the jury list of 1892; the first petroleum refinery at Nadwórna in 1900; the sawmill; the ironworks lease at Pasieczna in 1912 where Berish Rapaport is given the signature; the great fire of 1907 with Leizor collecting for the homeless; the 2,500 wagons a year and the exports as far as China; the refinery fire of 1923; Eisig Chaim elected fifth to the Stanisławów kahal board in 1924 with 2,175 votes; three sons’ engagements announced by their own clerks; the strike of 1926; the anonymous letter with a skull; and then July 1930, when it all came down — eleven million złoty of debt, widows and orphans who had trusted the firm more than the banks, the family leaving town days before the filing, Eisig Chaim dead in a Kraków prison that October, a five-year composition in which the administrators collected over a million and a half and the creditors got about a hundred thousand, workers unpaid for twenty-three months, two brothers beaten in the street outside the courthouse, and an acquittal in February 1936. And alongside all of it the other brother’s house holding: Zygmunt Griffel of Lwów, 60,000 tonnes of timber to England in one year, orange crates to Palestine, boycott sheets naming him as a Jew not to be traded with, ten thousand złoty given to Poland’s air-defence loan in March 1939, and the state taking his sawmill in 1946.

decoded_fields.notices: 142, every one translated in full into English and Hebrew with the Polish or German original beside it
decoded_fields.earliest: Gazeta Lwowska, 31 July 1866 — Griffel Benjamin, Griffel Chaim Samuel and Griffel Taube of Nadwórna give to the Israelite Patriotic Central Committee’s war fund during the Austro-Prussian War
decoded_fields.latest: Rzeszów voivodeship gazette, 21 November 1946 — the steam sawmill and box factory at Zarszyn, belonging to Zygmunt Griffel of Lwów, passes to the communist state
decoded_fields.our_own_line: Berish Rapaport appears twice: in the register entry of 31 October 1912 he is given procuration in the Griffel-Schwarz ironworks lease at Pasieczna, and in June 1913 the drilling journal Ropa reports a new oil company at Pasieczna called "Griffel jun. et Rappaport"
decoded_fields.the_four_brothers: The trial reports of 1935 name Eisig Chaim Griffel’s sons and their jobs: Szulim in the Stanisławów head office, JAKÓB running the Korneuburg refinery in Austria, Mendel on the technical side, Ozjasz Henryk in his father’s office. That is the sibling group on the wartime rescue list.
decoded_fields.the_three_engagements: Chwila announces Jakób Griffel to Fela FREILICH (1924), Mendel Griffel to Lucja AJCHENBAUM of Lublin (1925), and Szalom Griffel to Rega FORTGANG (1926) — all three surnames appear on the rescue list, and Rega answers the "Regi…" torn off its right edge.

title.en: David in the school register — printed student lists of the First State Gymnasium, Stanisławów, 1925/26 to 1928/29
title.he: דוד ברשימת התלמידים — רשימות התלמידים המודפסות של הגימנסיה הממלכתית הראשונה, סטניסלבוב, 1925/26 עד 1928/29
title.pl: Dawid w wykazie uczniów — Sprawozdania Dyrekcji I. Gimnazjum Państwowego im. M. Romanowskiego w Stanisławowie, 1925/26-1928/29
title.fr: David dans le registre scolaire — listes d’élèves du 1er Gymnase d’État, Stanisławów, 1925/26 à 1928/29

documents.summary_en:
Since 6 August this archive has said that the First State Gymnasium in Stanisławów is "where David was a pupil". It held the school’s annual reports, but not the student lists, so the statement was an inference. The lists are now here, and they carry his name three years running: Klasa IV in 1925/26, Klasa IVa in 1926/27 written out as "Rapaport Mendel Dawid", and Klasa Vb in 1927/28. He was born on 25 December 1911, so that is ages thirteen to sixteen. What was an assumption is now a printed record.

He is not on the 1928/29 list, and that is what Basia’s note refers to. Why he left after Klasa V — a change of school, a move, the family’s circumstances, or something else — no source here says. It is written down as a question rather than guessed at, and Basia has been asked to confirm that the sentence was meant about that one year.

decoded_fields.1926_27: KLASA IVa (29), group a — "Rapaport MENDEL DAWID", under both his given names.
decoded_fields.1928_29: Not present. Basia’s covering note reads "Dawid Rapaport is not on the list of students", and it follows the 1928/29 heading.
decoded_fields.also_on_these_pages: KLASA V of 1926/27 carries "Finder false Rapaport Chaim" and KLASA VI of 1927/28 "Finder f. Rapaport Chaim" — a different person, recorded here so nobody later mistakes him for ours.

title.en: Arolsen tracing index card — Lea Rapaport née Weitzner, document pulled 17 December 1970
title.he: כרטיס אינדקס של ארכיון ארולזן — לאה רפפורט לבית ויצנר, המסמך נשלף ב-17 בדצמבר 1970
title.pl: Karta indeksowa Arolsen — Lea Rapaport z domu Weitzner, dokument wyjęty 17 grudnia 1970
title.fr: Fiche d’index Arolsen — Lea Rapaport née Weitzner, document sorti le 17 décembre 1970

documents.summary_en:
An index card from the tracing service at Arolsen. It is not a record of Lusia’s life; it is a record of somebody LOOKING FOR IT. The card names her exactly as her own Displaced Persons card does — Lea Rapaport, born Weitzner, 8 April 1916, father Elias, mother Mathilde — which is what finally convinced Basia the two belonged together.

Two things on it are worth more than the rest.

FIRST, THE FIELDS ARE SWAPPED. "Geb.-Datum" — date of birth — contains the word Haifa. "Geb.-Ort" — place of birth — contains 8.4.1916. A clerk has put the place in the date box and the date in the place box. This archive has carried an open question about why Lusia’s DP card says she was born in Haifa when she was born in Bolechów. This is a second document carrying the same Haifa, and the first evidence that the two fields have been mishandled by somebody along the way. It does not settle the question. It changes what kind of question it is.

SECOND, ONLY ONE BOX IS TICKED. The card lists the sorts of record the file might contain — IRO identity card, IRO case card, Fiche Individuelle, an Italian card, a Schwabing card, an AJDC Belsen card, a CCLJ card. Only DP Karten is marked. So as far as this card goes, the DP card is the only thing the tracing service held for her, and she was not in the Belsen or Italian files. A blank with a reason is worth keeping.

"Entnommen am 17.12.1970" means the document was taken out of the file on 17 December 1970. Files were pulled when somebody asked for them. Nobody in this family knows who asked, or why, twenty-five years after the war.

decoded_fields.geb_datum_field_contains: Haifa  (the PLACE, written in the DATE box)
decoded_fields.geb_ort_field_contains: 8.4.1916  (the DATE, written in the PLACE box)
